name: Lam Wai-ying
current_role: Chair and 49% co-owner, Biel Crystal (HK) Manufactory, Hong Kong
profile: Hong Kong billionaire who co-founded and chairs Biel Crystal with her husband Yeung Kin-man (who holds 51% and is CEO). Biel is a leading maker of cover glass for smartphones, tablets and watches, supplying Apple, Samsung and Sony with a huge workforce in mainland China; IPO filings since 2021 have not materialised.
interesting_fact: Forbes ranked her the 67th most powerful woman in the world in 2017, and she has been listed among the richest self-made women globally.
notes: Very private; almost no interviews by her personally. Husband Yeung Kin-man is the public face. Company-listed media contact (Huizhou) is the best route; general info@ for HQ.

name: Heinz- George Baus
profile: Founder of German DIY/home-improvement chain Bauhaus (first store Mannheim, 1960). Died 10 May 2016.
notes: Died 10 May 2016 per Wikipedia and DIY International obituary (https://diyinternational.com/content/news/2016/05/20/bauhaus-founder-heinz-georg-baus-passes-away.html; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz-Georg_Baus). Son Bernd Baus is a Bauhaus managing director.

name: Daniel Mate
current_role: Retired former head of zinc/lead at Glencore (retired July 2020); private investor and Glencore shareholder
profile: Basque-born (San Sebastián) metals trader with economics and law degrees from Deusto. Joined Marc Rich & Co. in Madrid at 25, moved to Switzerland, took part in the 1994 management buyout that created Glencore and ran its zinc, copper and lead business until retiring in July 2020. Since then invests in Spanish real estate; lives in Switzerland.
interesting_fact: Through his property companies he bought Telefónica's former landmark Barcelona headquarters (Portal de l'Àngel/Fontanella), where Telefónica remains as a tenant.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Marc Rich & Co.'s Madrid office at age 25; after moving to the Swiss head office, Marc Rich himself took him on as a protégé. He also was a director of Asturiana de Zinc.
notes: Extremely low-profile (Forbes España notes even photos of him are hard to find). No published personal or office contacts found; Glencore media relations would not represent him post-retirement.

name: Yu Hao
profile: Born 1987, Yu Hao studied in Tsinghua University's aerospace school and founded Dreame Technology in 2017 with Xiaomi/Shunwei seed money (RMB 14m). Dreame grew from high-speed motors and robot vacuums into a global smart-home brand in 120+ countries and is now pushing into kitchens, appliances and a 'human-car-home' ecosystem.
interesting_fact: Yu says Dreame averaged roughly 100% annual revenue growth for eight straight years, and he has publicly set a (much-debated) goal of building a company worth RMB 100 trillion.
deep_cut_fact: In 2009, as a 22-year-old Tsinghua aerospace grad student, he founded the student club 'Sky Workshop' (天空工场) in a 20 m² dorm room; he is credited as an early Chinese quadcopter developer and inventor of a tricopter, and in 2026 his foundation relaunched 'Sky Workshop' as a youth-innovator grant program.
notes: Outspoken and media-friendly (long LatePost interview, personal social media videos). Press email is the media contact named on a Dreame CES 2026 release; other release-specific Dreame PR contacts exist.

name: Stephen Butt
current_role: President of Shareholder Relations and of the Central Market division, H-E-B; H-E-B board member
profile: Great-grandson of H-E-B founder Florence Butt and nephew of chairman Charles Butt, Stephen Butt is a member of the family that owns privately held Texas grocer H-E-B (Texas and Mexico, roughly $50bn revenue). Based in Dallas, he runs H-E-B's specialty-food Central Market format and shareholder relations and sits on the board.
interesting_fact: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity. The first Central Market opened in Austin on 22 Jan 1994 despite advice that a store without Coke, Pepsi or Tide would fail.
deep_cut_fact: He recalls that in Central Market's second year, shoppers began carpooling from Houston and Dallas with big coolers, taking turns filling friends' shopping lists; by year three customers routinely drove 25 miles to shop there.
notes: Described by PaperCity as a 'low-key billionaire' who 'doesn't want press'. He did give Shelby Report and Dallas Morning News interviews tied to Central Market, so pitching around Central Market/food retail innovation works best via H-E-B public affairs. Note: H-E-B's CEO is not his brother (Forbes bio claim looks outdated/wrong); verify before citing.

name: Wang Yun‘an
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Guming Holdings (Good me / 古茗), HKEX: 1364
profile: Millennial founder (born mid-1980s) of Good me, a franchise bubble-tea chain he started in 2010 after graduating from Zhejiang Sci-Tech University. Focused on lower-tier Chinese towns and cities, it grew to roughly 10,000 stores; Guming listed in Hong Kong in Feb 2025, making him a billionaire. HQ Hangzhou.
interesting_fact: The first Good me shop opened in April 2010 in Daxi town, Wenling (Taizhou), Zhejiang, opened with a high-school friend; the name 古茗 means roughly 'old tea'. Big-city tea brands hadn't reached small towns yet, which was his opening.
deep_cut_fact: As a student he sold radios and quilts and helped classmates sign up for credit cards, building up hundreds of thousands of yuan; after graduating he lasted just two weeks as a car-dealership (4S store) salesman in Hangzhou before quitting to open his tea shop.
notes: Rarely gives interviews. Company site lists a named media contact (媒体联系) and brand-partnership email; IR page at gumingnc.com/investors.

name: Ricardo Martin Bringas
current_role: CEO (Director General) and board member, Organización Soriana (Mexico)
profile: Member of the Martín Bringas family that controls Soriana, one of Mexico's largest supermarket chains (founded in Torreón). A 1982 Tec de Monterrey computer-systems graduate, he worked across commercial, credit, finance and systems roles before becoming director general on 4 Nov 1991, a post he has held for 30+ years.
interesting_fact: He has run Soriana as CEO since November 1991, one of the longest CEO tenures among Mexico's listed companies.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2025 Tec de Monterrey's Laguna campus gave him the Premio al Mérito EXATEC; accepting it he said 'success is a very subjective word' and advised young entrepreneurs to act with ethics, professionalism and 'mucho empuje' (lots of drive).
notes: Low media profile. IR email is from Soriana's BMV issuer profile and may be dated; confirm via Soriana's investor site.

name: Sara George
current_role: Director, St. George's School (Alaknanda, New Delhi) and Paul George Global School; shareholder in Muthoot Finance
profile: Dr. Sara George Muthoot is an educationist and a major shareholder of Kerala-founded gold-loan lender Muthoot Finance, inheriting a stake after her husband, group chairman M.G. George Muthoot, died in 2021. She has long directed the Muthoot Group's Delhi schools and has been the only Malayali woman on the Forbes billionaires list.
interesting_fact: St. George's School, founded in 1962 by an Orthodox priest, came under the Muthoot Group in 1982; the school credits her 'untiring efforts' as director for turning a small, little-known school into one of Delhi's notable schools.
deep_cut_fact: The school quotes her philosophy: 'Each child is as important to us as if he or she were our own. We are not interested in academic statistics alone.' She received an 'Excellence in Instructional Leadership' award at the 2022 Educational Excellence Conclave.
notes: Private; not an operating executive of Muthoot Finance. Route via her school (St. George's School office) is most direct. Avoid referencing family tragedies (husband's 2021 death, son's 2009 death).

name: Sylvan Adams
current_role: President, World Jewish Congress Israel (since 2025); owner of Iberville Developments; philanthropist
profile: Quebec City-born (1958) real-estate heir who ran and later became sole owner of Canada's Iberville Developments, founded by his father Marcel. Emigrated to Tel Aviv in 2015 and became one of Israel's best-known philanthropists (Giving Pledge), funding sport, medicine and education, including a $100m gift in 2025 to rebuild a missile-struck hospital. Stepped back from his cycling team in late 2025.
interesting_fact: He personally funded bringing the 2018 Giro d'Italia start to Israel, the first time any Grand Tour stage was held outside Europe, and built the Middle East's first indoor velodrome in Tel Aviv.
deep_cut_fact: He only took up cycling in his 40s, yet won a Masters world title in Manchester in 2017 and has been a multiple-time Masters world time-trial champion in his age category; he also donated $2m to redevelop the Bromont Velodrome in Quebec.
notes: High public profile in Israel; frequently interviewed by Jewish/Israeli and cycling media. No self-published email/socials verified; best route is via World Jewish Congress Israel or the Margaret and Sylvan Adams Family Foundation. Israel–Premier Tech controversy (renamed for 2026) is sensitive; avoid leading with it.
